newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Marcos victims demand $1.9 billion in damages.
newsitem.headline: Marcos victims demand $1.9 billion in damages.

text.p: Victims of human rights abuses during the rule of late Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos asked a Manila court on Wednesday to order the Marcos family to pay $1.9 billion in damages awarded them by a U.S. federal jury.

Five Filipinos, including a Roman Catholic nun, filed the class action before a judge in Manila's Makati business district on behalf of about 9,500 victims and relatives of victims of torture, killings and disappearances under Marcos's government.

The victims' chief Filipino lawyer, Rod Domingo, said in a statement that the action to collect on the judgment issued in favour of the victims by a federal jury in Hawaii was "a real acid test on (the Philippine) justice system."
"It is now up to the courts to show the world that indeed our justice system is not the best money can buy," he added.
The Hawaii jury awarded the judgement in 1994 and a U.S. appeals court last December upheld the award.
A spokeswoman for former first lady Imelda Marcos told Reuters that the widow of the former president had no immediate comment, but might issue a statement on Thursday.
The victims, in their suit, asked the judge to declare the Hawaii jury's verdict as "a valid foreign judgement enforceable in the Philippines" and to enforce it.
Marcos died in exile in Hawaii in 1989, three years after he was overthrown in a popular revolt that ended his 20-year rule.
The Philippine government is also after the Marcoses' money, accusing Marcos, his wife and associates of stealing up to $5 billion from the economy during his rule.
The family has denied the charges, saying Marcos's assets came from his earnings as a lawyer before he became president.
Mrs Marcos, now a member of the Congress, was convicted of corruption by a Manila court in 1993 and sentenced to 18 years in jail. She is out on bail while the case is on appeal.
